settings.headline: Getting there, getting in,
settings.subtitle: Driftwood Point is a car-light site. The easiest way in is the free shuttle from Halcyon Bay station.

items.title: Shuttle
items.text: Free buses every 10 minutes from Halcyon Bay station, 11 am until 1:30 am. Step-free, with space for wheelchairs.

items.title: Bike or walk
items.text: The Beach Gate is a 25-minute walk along the boardwalk, with free parking for 2,000 bikes.

items.title: Car
items.text: 1,500 spaces at $25 a day, and they sell out. Car-share spaces are $10. Book with your tickets.

items.title: What to bring
items.text: An empty bottle, sunscreen, a small bag (under 30 by 40 cm), a blanket. No glass, umbrellas or drones.

items.title: Cashless
items.text: Every trader takes cards and phones. Cash-to-card is at the Info tent.

items.title: Looking after you
items.text: Paramedics at First Aid all day, free water at two refill stations and a quiet welfare space.

settings.headline: A festival that works
settings.body:
Main paths are matting or boardwalk, and every stage has step-free access. The accessible viewing platform at the Tidepool Main Stage has seats and space for wheelchairs, with room for one companion each.

If you need a companion to attend, their ticket is free. ASL interpreters sign every headline set on the screens, and you can request interpreters for other sets until July 1.

Write to access@lowtide.example with anything else you need. A person reads every email.
